# platform-probe

> A small, dependency-free Go status page for the Meddleware platform. It probes
> internal health endpoints server-side on a timer, caches an aggregated,
> capability-grouped snapshot, and serves it to browsers, which only ever read the
> cache. The snapshot is topology-free (no internal URLs/hostnames). Runs on
> `scratch` as non-root UID 65534.

## Purpose

- Show end-to-end health of user-facing capabilities, grouped (Identity & Access,
  Container Registry, …), not a flat list of hostnames.
- Probe server-side and cache the result so clients read a cheap snapshot and probe
  load is independent of visitor count.
- Assert real conditions (status code / body), so status reflects health, not mere
  reachability.

## Endpoints

- `GET /api/status` — cached JSON snapshot: {generated_at, overall, groups[]}.
- `GET /healthz` — 200 liveness (independent of probed dependencies).
- CLI: `-healthcheck` dials /healthz and exits 0/1 (container HEALTHCHECK).

## Configuration (environment variables)

- `PORT` (default 8080)
- `PROBE_INTERVAL` (default 15s) — cycle period + snapshot freshness
- `PROBE_TIMEOUT` (default 5s) — per-probe timeout; must be < PROBE_INTERVAL
- `CHECKS_CONFIG_FILE` (default /etc/platform-probe/checks.json) — the probe targets,
  re-read every cycle
- `LOG_LEVEL` (default info)

## Behaviour

- Prober goroutine probes all checks concurrently each cycle; component = condition
  met ? operational : down. Rollup: all operational → operational, all down → down,
  mixed → degraded (components → group, groups → overall).
- Checks are loaded at runtime from CHECKS_CONFIG_FILE (in the cluster a mounted,
  SOPS-encrypted Secret); no probe targets are compiled into the binary or image, and
  URLs never reach clients. Only config.example.json (dummy example.com entries) is in
  the repo.
- A check passes on its expect_status (exact); with no expect_status only a 2xx passes.
  Redirects are not followed. Point a check at an endpoint that exercises the whole
  dependency chain so a 200 proves more than reachability.
- This is a JSON API only: the status page UI is the separate status-page SPA.

## Security invariants

- Topology-free API: no URLs, hostnames, ports, or error text in any response.
- Server-side + cached: clients never trigger a probe.
- Fail safe to down on any probe error/timeout/mismatch (including a non-2xx for a
  check without expect_status); never panic.

## Supply chain

- Multi-arch images (amd64/arm64) on quay.io + Docker Hub.
- SBOM (SPDX) + SLSA provenance attached; keyless cosign signatures over the digest.
- Base image pinned by digest; reproducible build; standard library only (no deps).
